en.title: Japan's Hokkaido Records Best Potato Harvest in a Decade
en.dek: Hokkaido produced 250,000 tons of potatoes, the highest in ten years, amid global crop failures.
facts: The region accounts for 80% of Japan’s potato production.
Only Hokkaido increased production in the Northern Hemisphere.
Hokkaido had four days above 86°F, compared with sixteen last year.
No deluges occurred, reducing pest risk.
body: Good News Network reports that Hokkaido produced 250,000 tons of potatoes, matching the region’s usual quota. The figure represents the highest harvest in a decade. The island supplies 80% of Japan’s potato supply. The data comes from Calbee, a major potato product manufacturer.

The report notes that worldwide crop failures have been driven by rising summer temperatures and droughts. France and Italy have seen declines in harvest volume and quality. Japan’s Hokkaido is the only Northern Hemisphere region that increased production this year.

Hokkaido’s capital, Sapporo, recorded only four days above 86°F, compared with sixteen such days last year. Cooler autumn temperatures helped potatoes form denser, spherical shapes. The firmer ground improved machinery access, and the cooler climate extended storage life.

The region did not experience deluges that could trigger pest outbreaks. Good News Network compares the harvest to a recent "potato flood" in Germany, where millions of potatoes were given away. The event underscores the impact of climate uncertainty on agriculture.
en.context: Rising summer temperatures and extended droughts have battered traditional agricultural powerhouses like southern France and northern Italy, according to Good News Network. The article highlights that Japan’s Hokkaido region is the only Northern Hemisphere area that increased production this year.
